Sample Size Planning for a Mean From the Accuracy in Parameter Estimation (AIPE) Perspective

Source: R/ss_aipe_mean.R
ss_aipe_mean.Rd

Plans the sample size N needed for the confidence interval for a population mean to be sufficiently narrow, from the accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) perspective. The mean may be that of a single sample or the mean of paired differences: in a pretest-posttest or matched pairs design each unit contributes one difference score, the interval for the mean difference is the single sample interval computed on those scores, and the plan is the same with true_sd the standard deviation of the differences. Without an assurance the plan makes the expected width of the interval no wider than width; with one, it makes the realized width no wider than width with that probability.

Usage

ss_aipe_mean(
  true_sd,
  width,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  true_kurtosis = 0
)

Arguments

true_sd

The planning value of the population standard deviation of the scores whose mean is estimated. For a paired design it is the standard deviation of the differences, which for two measures with standard deviations \(\sigma_1\) and \(\sigma_2\) and correlation \(\rho\) is \(\sqrt{\sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2 - 2\rho\,\sigma_1\sigma_2}\). Must be positive.

width

The desired full width of the confidence interval (twice its half-width), in the units of the scores.

conf_level

The confidence level of the interval (default 0.95).

assurance

NULL (the default) to plan the expected width, or the desired probability, strictly between 0.5 and 1, that the realized width will be no wider than width.

true_kurtosis

The planning value of the population excess kurtosis of the scores, on the scale kurtosis reports (0 for a normal population). It enters only the assurance adjustment (see Details). The default 0 is normal theory. The value must be greater than -2: no distribution has an excess kurtosis below -2, and only a population of two equally likely values reaches it. A pilot's kurtosis() can usually be passed as it is, but kurtosis() corrects its estimate for small-sample bias, and for a pilot whose scores take nearly two values it can return -2 or less (kurtosis(rep(c(0, 1), 123)) is about -2.016), which is refused. Such a pilot says the population is close to that two-valued limit. Pass instead a value a little above -2, such as -1.9, or 0, the normal theory plan, which for an assurance of .80 or more is never the smaller of the two.

Value

A data.frame of class dmar_ss_aipe with columns term and value and the rows necessary_N (the planned sample size), expected_width (the expected width of the interval at that size under normality), the input echoes true_sd, width, and conf_level, and, when an assurance was supplied, assurance and true_kurtosis.

Details

The interval. The \(100(1 - \alpha)\)% interval for the mean is \(\bar{y} \pm t_{1-\alpha/2,\,N-1}\, S/\sqrt{N}\), the interval t.test() reports for a single sample and for paired data. Its full width \(W = 2\, t_{1-\alpha/2,\,N-1}\, S/\sqrt{N}\) is random because the sample standard deviation \(S\) is, so a plan is a statement either about the expected width or about the probability that \(W\) is no larger than the desired width \(\omega\). These are the two criteria Kelley and Rausch (2006) developed for the standardized mean difference and that Kelley, Maxwell, and Rausch (2003) developed for the unstandardized mean difference.

Expected width. Without an assurance, necessary_N is the smallest N at which $$E(W) = 2\, t_{1-\alpha/2,\,N-1}\, c_4(N)\, \sigma / \sqrt{N} \le \omega,$$ where, under normality, $$c_4(N) = \frac{E(S)}{\sigma} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{N - 1}}\, \frac{\Gamma(N/2)}{\Gamma((N - 1)/2)}.$$ The expected width is therefore exact under normality. It falls as N rises, so the criterion, once met, holds at every larger N. The expected_width row reports it at necessary_N.

How the plan differs from ss_aipe_c(). ss_aipe_c(), which plans a contrast among independent groups, sets \(S\) equal to \(\sigma\) in the width. Because \(E(S) = c_4(N)\,\sigma < \sigma\), the width it plans is larger than the expected width, and the same rule applied to a single mean gives either the N returned here or one more. With an assurance the difference disappears: the criterion is then the probability that \(S\) is small enough, which does not involve \(E(S)\), and under normality it is the criterion ss_aipe_c() uses for a contrast, here applied to a single mean. (ss_aipe_c() cannot plan a single mean, since it requires contrast weights that sum to zero.)

Assurance. With assurance \(\gamma\), necessary_N is the smallest N from which \(P(W \le \omega) \ge \gamma\) holds at every larger N. Because \(W \le \omega\) exactly when $$\frac{S^2}{\sigma^2} \le \frac{N \omega^2}{4\, t^2_{1-\alpha/2,\,N-1}\, \sigma^2},$$ the probability is that of \(S^2\) falling below a bound. Under normality \((N - 1) S^2/\sigma^2\) is chi square on \(N - 1\) degrees of freedom, so the probability is exact, and the criterion, once met, holds at every larger N; necessary_N is then simply the smallest N at which \(P(W \le \omega) \ge \gamma\). The two readings part only under the kurtosis adjustment (see below).

Kurtosis. For N independent scores whose excess kurtosis is \(\kappa\), the variance of the sample variance is $$\mathrm{Var}(S^2) = \sigma^4 \left\{\frac{2}{N - 1} + \frac{\kappa}{N}\right\},$$ against \(2\sigma^4/(N - 1)\) under normality. With a nonzero true_kurtosis the chi square law is replaced by a scaled chi square, \(S^2/\sigma^2 \approx \chi^2_\nu/\nu\), with $$\nu = \frac{2}{2/(N - 1) + \kappa/N}$$ chosen so that the approximation has the exact mean and variance of \(S^2/\sigma^2\); \(\nu = N - 1\) when \(\kappa = 0\). Tails heavier than the normal's (\(\kappa > 0\)) make \(S\) more variable, and for an assurance of .80 or more they make it harder to reach, while lighter tails (\(\kappa < 0\), as for scores on a bounded scale) make it easier. Precisely, with an assurance of .80 or more, when the plan made with a given \(\kappa\) has at least \(\kappa + 3\) observations, no smaller planning value of \(\kappa\) gives a larger plan, so an overstated \(\kappa\) errs on the side of a larger N. With an assurance close to one half the criterion turns instead on the median of \(S^2\), which heavier tails pull further below \(\sigma^2\), and a larger \(\kappa\) can give a slightly smaller plan. The argument is on the excess scale of kurtosis, so kurtosis(pilot) can usually be passed as it is (see the true_kurtosis argument for a pilot that gives -2 or less). A pilot's kurtosis is itself imprecise. The kurtosis does not enter the expected width plan: there it would lower \(E(S)\) by a relative amount of about \(\kappa/(8N)\) and N by about \(\kappa/4\), less than one when \(|\kappa| < 4\), so the plan keeps normal theory's \(c_4(N)\) and the function warns when a nonzero true_kurtosis is supplied without an assurance.

The two-moment approximation is coarse when \(\kappa\) is large and N is small. Once N is below about \(\kappa/2\), \(\nu\) is below one, and the smaller \(\nu\) is, the more of the scaled chi square's probability sits near zero, much as most small samples from a population with heavy tails miss the tails. The probability can then meet the assurance at a very small N, fall below it over a stretch of larger N, and meet it again. This is where the definition above matters: necessary_N is the start of the stretch over which the criterion holds at every larger N, not the first N at which it holds, and in this region a larger \(\kappa\) can give a smaller plan. The function finds that N exactly: it bounds the criterion over whole ranges of N, using only that \(\nu\) and the bound on \(S^2/\sigma^2\) both rise with N and that a chi square quantile rises with its degrees of freedom, and evaluates it directly where the bounds cannot decide. ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity(), with a pilot's scores as the population, checks a plan without the approximation, and it also shows the coverage of the t interval under the shape of those scores, which the plan does not address.

When no planning value is trustworthy. A fixed N is only as good as the planning value of \(\sigma\). Sequential fixed-width confidence interval procedures for a mean keep sampling until the interval reaches the target width and need no planning value of \(\sigma\).

References

Kelley, K., Maxwell, S. E., & Rausch, J. R. (2003). Obtaining power or obtaining precision: Delineating methods of sample-size planning. Evaluation & the Health Professions, 26(3), 258–287. doi:10.1177/0163278703255242

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Examples

# A pilot: the IQ gains (end of year minus pretest) of the 246 children
# in the control group of the pygmalion data. A gain is a paired
# difference, so its mean is planned as a single mean.
gain <- pygmalion$iq_gain[pygmalion$treatment == "Control"]
sd(gain)
#> [1] 13.29708
kurtosis(gain)
#> [1] 1.196691

# The N at which the expected full width of the 95 percent interval for
# the mean gain is at most 4 IQ points.
ss_aipe_mean(true_sd = sd(gain), width = 4)
#>  term           value 
#>  necessary_N    172   
#>  expected_width 3.997 
#>  true_sd        13.297
#>  width          4     
#>  conf_level     0.950 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# With 90 percent assurance that the realized width is at most 4 points,
# first under normal theory and then with the heavier than normal tails
# the pilot shows.
ss_aipe_mean(true_sd = sd(gain), width = 4, assurance = 0.90)
#>  term           value 
#>  necessary_N    195   
#>  expected_width 3.751 
#>  true_sd        13.297
#>  width          4     
#>  conf_level     0.950 
#>  assurance      0.900 
#>  true_kurtosis  0.000 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
ss_aipe_mean(true_sd = sd(gain), width = 4, assurance = 0.90,
             true_kurtosis = kurtosis(gain))
#>  term           value 
#>  necessary_N    201   
#>  expected_width 3.694 
#>  true_sd        13.297
#>  width          4     
#>  conf_level     0.950 
#>  assurance      0.900 
#>  true_kurtosis  1.197 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
